title: Capacity shelf mapping and surge annotations — weeknotes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from this week’s capacity shelf mapping exercise and surge annotations for EMEA / APAC west-edge. This is a working doc (not final). Intended to capture: heuristics we used to place buffer nodes, open questions for SRE/Capacity, and immediate handoff checklist for next oncall rotation.

TL;DR:
- Ran a 36-hour shelf-mapping pass across eu-west, ap-south, and us-west.
- Identified two medium-risk shelves (eu-west-b and ap-south-2) where contention spikes during nightly batch jobs reduce burst capacity by ~17%.
- Proposed short-term mitigation: pre-warm 8 x A100-v5 equivalents in ap-south-2 between 01:00–05:00 local to absorb scheduled backlog.
- Longer-term: add scheduling constraint to batch pipeline to spread across shelves to avoid correlated preemption.

Raw observations (notes-to-self style):
- eu-west-b: queue depth correlates with internal nightly embed job (team: search-relevance). Surges predictable 02:30–03:45 UTC. When we prime, priming latency improves but eviction rate increases in adjacent low-priority pools.
- ap-south-2: vendor reported maintenance window last week, we observed slightly elevated preemptions on p3-class nodes. Our transient pool loses 12–18% capacity in sim.
- us-west-edge: stable for user-facing hosted API; but burst patterns show larger variance (10–90th percentile) during promo events.

Capacity shelf mapping (heuristic rules applied):
- Shelf classification: green (>=20% spare), amber (5-20% spare), red (<5% spare). Spare measured as conservatively available vGPU-hrs for the next 72h based on forecast model v4.
- Move ephemeral burst capacity to amber shelves where region-local replication exists (prefer eu-west-a over eu-west-b).

Listing (compact):
- eu-west-a: green — keep as primary burst pool, 12% of dedicated spare to be kept for canary rollouts.
- eu-west-b: amber — mark for nightly pre-warm; target +8 nodes (A100-v5 equiv).
- ap-south-1: green — OK.
- ap-south-2: amber -> suggested pre-warm 8 nodes 01:00–05:00 IST; add alert if preemptions > 5 in 15m window.
- us-west-edge: green but noisy — add telemetry for promo tagging, consider short-term reserve of 4 nodes during scheduled marketing events.

Experiment runs this week (what we tried):
- Controlled pre-warm in eu-west-b (2027-04-11 00:00–09:00 UTC): pre-warm reduced cold-start latencies by 42% but caused a 6% increase in preemptive evictions in adjacent low-priority pools — observed as increased retries in batch jobs.
- Localized KV-cache warmup: demo'd reduced token compute by 9% at 95th percentile; requires runtime flags to be persisted per shelf.

Open questions / risks to call out:
1) Scheduling constraint ripple: If we throttle nightly embed pipeline to spread across shelves, will that increase total job completion time beyond SLA for internal consumers? Need input from search-relevance (cc: @Mateo).
2) Billing impact of pre-warming — finance needs a quick estimate for keeping 8 nodes warm nightly for month (rough order of magnitude).
3) Alert fatigue: propose a composite alert (preemptions * eviction_rate) rather than firing on simple preemption spikes.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- (Priya) Draft short-term pre-warm runbook for ap-south-2 and eu-west-b: include start/stop commands, expected cost delta, rollback steps (due 2027-04-14).
- (Evan) Add promo-tags telemetry pipeline for us-west-edge and surface in Console (due 2027-04-15).
- (Rashmi) Model update: re-run forecast v4 with new batch schedule; output expected spare delta for 30/60/90 day horizons (due 2027-04-16).
- (Samira) Finance ask: estimate incremental cost of nightly pre-warm (due 2027-04-15).

Handoff checklist for next oncall (short, copy into handoff doc):
- Check pre-warm job statuses at 01:00 local for ap-south-2 and eu-west-b.
- Verify eviction composite alert thresholds haven't tripped. If tripped: pause pre-warm and notify search-relevance.
- If batch job spread is below target on eu-west-b, escalate to Mateo for schedule rebalance.

Notes for runbook (rough snippets to paste into confluence):
- Pre-warm CLI: fleetctl shelf prewarm --region ap-south-2 --count 8 --instance-type a100-v5 --ttl 4h --label surge-role=priming
- Rollback: fleetctl shelf drain --region <region> --labels surge-role=priming --grace 600
- Cost calc: hourly_cost * nodes * hours_per_night * nights_per_month (use k8s-finance rate card in linked artifacts)

Incidents/Anomalies this week:
- 2027-04-10 03:10 UTC: transient 5m spike in eu-west-b causing 502s for small percent of hosted API traffic. Root cause: uncoordinated kernel update on vendor infra; mitigation: re-route critical tenant traffic to eu-west-a for 12 hrs. Ticket: INFRA-4809.

Loose ideas (brainstorm):
- Consider per-tenant priming budgets for high-SLA customers so they can pay for hot nodes during promo windows.
- Build a pre-warm simulator in staging that can predict eviction spillover using synthetic batch traces.

References / Links:
- Forecast model v4 runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=83291
- Related jira: INFRA-4827 (shelf mapping), INFRA-4809 (eu-west-b 502s)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-config/pull/214 (adds shelf labels and prewarm cron)

Unresolved TODOs (for next sync):
- Coordinate with Search-Relevance and Batch owners to get non-overlapping maintenance windows for the next 8 weeks.
- Finalize composite alert definition and add to the Console dashboards.

Quick retrospective note:
This week’s mapping pass felt productive — having a small, focused triage window (36 hours) helped us find shelf-level contention that global metrics were smoothing over. Need better tooling to tie batch job IDs to shelf traces.

End of doc — ephemeral working notes (will move final runbook bits to Confluence after next review).
